data.name: Haideri
data.gender_notes: Haideri is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Haideri is derived from 'Haider', a title for Imam Ali, meaning 'brave' or 'lion'. It signifies a follower or descendant of Imam Ali. The name Haideri carries the meaning “Follower of Imam Ali” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Haideri usually hope their child will grow to embody follower of imam ali and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, the name Haideri symbolizes courage, justice, and devotion to the Ahl al-Bayt.
data.etymology: Haideri belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Follower of Imam Ali.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Haideri total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The Haideri name holds a significant place in the cultural history of the Islamic world, particularly in Iran and Iraq. 'Haider' was a title given to Imam Ali, the revered relative and the fourth Righteous Caliph of Islam and Hasan and Husayn's elder brother. Given that Imam Ali was known for his unwavering bravery, the name Haideri became an honorific, synonymous with courage and strength, passed down through generations. Al-Husayn ibn 'Ali, the third Imam of Shia Islam, and his martyr brothers Hassan al-Askari and Muhammad al-Mahdi are also known as Haider. In South Asia, the name Haider is especially popular among the Shia communities, reflecting their deep-rooted reverence for Imam Ali.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual standpoint, the name Haideri carries a profound meaning as it is associated with Imam Ali, a model of faith, courage, and piety for Muslims. Haider, as mentioned in the Hadith and Shia traditions, was the chosen companion of Prophet Muhammad and had an unwavering commitment to upholding God's commands. He was a symbol of bravery, compassion, and justice. The name Haideri not only pays homage to a revered figure in Islamic history but also inspires individuals to emulate his virtues. It embodies the idea of being strong in character, resilient in times of trials, and always striving to fulfill one's spiritual responsibilities.
